edition.alertText: Rubio at G7: 'no need for major combat operations' — economic campaign 'so devastating' that military action unnecessary; Trump holds off strikes 'for the time being,' posts 'positive momentum' on social media; Iran's Araghchi: conflict 'will not be resolved through military means'; Rezaei posts 'FOLD YOUR HAND' on X; ADNOC vessel damaged in attack in UAE territorial waters — response ongoing; UKMTO: tanker struck by unknown projectile 19nm NE of Lima, Oman — crew safe; IRGC claims two tankers caught fire after 'massive explosions' in Hormuz — one supertanker hit naval mine; IRGC claims third tanker struck mine in eastern Hormuz; Iran says US coastal radar systems in southern strait 'destroyed'; oil extends slide — Brent settles $91.49 (-1.17%), WTI $86.04 (-0.93%), both at two-month lows; gold crashes 2.60% to $4,032 as hot CPI (Oct +0.4% vs +0.3% expected) lifts December Fed hike odds — 10Y Treasury near 4.94%; stocks reverse Monday's gains — Dow -0.30%, Nasdaq -0.74%; GCC states approve military command headquarters in Kuwait; France blames IRGC cyber unit for supermarket refrigeration hack, EU ready for 'united response'; Qatar PM makes surprise G7 stop in Paris to brief allies on Iran deal; Canada reimposed sanctions on 11 Iranian entities; Iraq reopens Sheeb border crossing with Iran; Saudi coalition intercepts 2 Houthi missiles toward Riyadh + drone over Eastern Province; explosions heard in Riyadh (AFP); US gas $4.01/gal (AAA); IMF PortWatch: only 3 Hormuz transits on Nov 8 vs 85/day baseline; 57 AIS-visible vessels holding position near strait; Qatar LNG loadings at ~half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg); Saudi tanker firm sends vessels through Hormuz with US coordination (Bloomberg)

situation: The Strait of Hormuz crisis entered day 257 as a pivot from military to economic warfare took shape. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking at the G7 foreign ministers' meeting in Paris on Tuesday, declared there was 'no need for major combat operations' against Iran, crediting the US economic campaign as 'so devastating' that military action was unnecessary. The statement marked the administration's clearest signal yet that the war's kinetic phase may be winding down — at least temporarily. Trump reinforced the message, saying he would hold off on strikes 'for the time being' and posting on social media that the US was seeing 'positive momentum toward an end to this Conflict.' The diplomatic thaw contrasted sharply with Tehran's defiance: Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told IRNA that the conflict 'will not be resolved through military means, nor by intensifying sanctions,' while security chief Mohsen Rezaei urged Washington to 'FOLD YOUR HAND' on X. Iran reiterated that its offer to reopen Hormuz within two days remains on the table, conditional on the US ending the war, unfreezing assets, lifting oil sanctions, and terminating the naval blockade. Qatar's Prime Minister made a surprise stop at the G7 in Paris to brief allies on the $8 billion deal framework, while the UK's Ed Miliband called for an 'all-out diplomatic effort,' warning the 'no war, no peace' stalemate was causing widespread economic pain. Meanwhile, GCC defense ministers meeting in Bahrain approved a military command headquarters in Kuwait — a step toward institutionalizing Gulf defense coordination. Canada reimposed sanctions on 11 Iranian entities over nuclear links, and Iraq reopened its Sheeb border crossing with Iran.

Markets reversed Monday's euphoria as a hot inflation print overshadowed the diplomatic optimism. October CPI came in at +0.4% month-over-month versus the +0.3% expected, with core CPI also beating at +0.3%, pulling a December Fed rate hike firmly into focus — markets now fully price a 25bp increase, with a 10.5% chance of 50bp. The 10-year Treasury yield surged toward 4.94%, while the 2-year approached 4.69%. Gold bore the brunt, crashing 2.60% to approximately $4,032/oz after Monday's $4,149 close, as the stronger dollar and rising yields eroded haven demand. Stocks surrendered their Monday rally — the Dow fell 0.30% to 52,232, the S&P 500 dropped 0.38%, and the Nasdaq lost 0.74%. Oil continued its slide, with Brent settling at $91.49/bbl (-1.17%) — briefly dipping below $90 intraday — and WTI at $86.04/bbl (-0.93%), both hitting their lowest levels since late August. Brent has now fallen roughly 22% from its October 30 peak of $117.64, as Trump's restraint signals and Rubio's economic-war stance further deflated the war-risk premium. Newcastle coal held near $144–145/tonne. The US national average gasoline price dipped to $4.01/gal (AAA, Nov 9), crossing below the $4 threshold that has been a political milestone throughout the conflict. VLCC rates for Arabian Gulf–China routes softened further to the $360K–400K/day range as continued oil weakness and easing war fears compressed shipping premiums.

Despite the diplomatic momentum, the maritime situation continued to deteriorate on Tuesday. An ADNOC Logistics & Services vessel was damaged in an attack in UAE territorial waters on Tuesday afternoon — the company said response efforts were ongoing but disclosed no details on the vessel's identity, damage extent, or crew injuries. ADNOC ships have been attacked repeatedly since the war began, with two struck in July (one crew member killed) and another in August. Separately, UKMTO reported a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile approximately 19 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman (Warning 201-26), with the master confirming all crew safe and a damage assessment planned for first light. The IRGC escalated its claims, reporting two oil tankers 'brought to a halt following massive explosions' — one a supertanker that struck a naval mine, the second under US escort attempting a 'covert passage via an illegal route.' Hours later, Iran's military reported a third tanker struck a mine in the eastern strait after 'violating the rules,' with smoke billowing over the waterway. The IRGC claimed US coastal radar and navigation equipment in the southern strait had been destroyed, forcing tankers onto unauthorized routes. IMF PortWatch recorded just 3 transits on November 8 versus the pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day, while Straits.live counted 57 AIS-visible vessels holding position near the strait. Bloomberg reported that a Saudi tanker firm was sending vessels through Hormuz with US military coordination, while Qatar LNG loadings picked up to roughly half of pre-war levels. The Saudi-led coalition intercepted two Houthi missiles fired toward Riyadh and a drone over the Eastern Province on Tuesday, with AFP journalists reporting explosions in the capital. France publicly blamed Iran's IRGC cyber unit for the October supermarket refrigeration hack that disrupted hundreds of stores, with the EU warning it was ready for a 'united response.'

supplyChain.name: Sulfur
supplyChain.text: Global exports down 39% YoY to 6.1M tonnes in Q2 (S&P). Sulfur prices above $1,000/tonne — more than doubled since pre-war — feeding into phosphate production costs; Egypt, Brazil, India cutting output. Mosaic phosphate plants remain curtailed including South Fort Meade (Florida) — 199 workers laid off. Morocco's OCP needs 3.7M tonnes/yr from the region. Nearly half of seaborne sulfur passed through Hormuz pre-war. Phosphate prices up 25-30%; DAP at $803/mt in October, ~30% above January (IFDC). Trade routes shifting as Morocco and China seek alternative sources (ChemAnalyst). China phosphate exports near zero in 2026, down from ~5.3M mt in 2025 (IFDC).

supplyChain.name: Sulfuric Acid
supplyChain.text: China banned exports Apr-Aug (700kt/yr quota replaced). SX-EW copper producers (15% of global cathode) fully exposed. Huayou cut Indonesian nickel HPAL output 50%.

supplyChain.name: Fertilizer
supplyChain.text: Fertilizer shipments through Hormuz at zero for fourth consecutive month — September, October, and early November all zero (World Visualized/Syz Group/Fertilizer Daily). Urea exports from Hormuz-dependent economies fell 83% YoY in April (ITC). ~850kt urea stranded. 4 of 5 Bangladesh urea plants shut since March due to LNG shortages. Pakistan faces 200,000-ton fertiliser shortfall (Express Tribune). FAO Food Price Index at 136 (highest since Nov 2022). World Bank: fertilizer prices surging as Hormuz disruptions tighten supplies. DAP at $803/mt in October, urea near January levels after April spike (IFDC Bulletin #37). Egypt gas supply cuts to fertilizer producers rose from 20% to 33% on Nov 8 — AGF Nitrogen running at 80-85% capacity (IFDC). Russia export quotas Dec 2026–May 2027 at ~18.8M mt, down from ~20M mt. European Commission: fertilizer-to-cereal price ratios at weakest since 2022. Urea-to-corn ratio at 126 bushels/tonne vs 75 in Dec 2025 (CSIS). IFPRI: no bypass route for ammonia or sulfur unlike crude. UN fertilizer corridor stalled pending US-Iran agreement. Fertilizer ships face long backlog even if Hormuz reopens — access not cost will define markets (Supply Chain Brain/World Fertilizer).

supplyChain.name: LNG
supplyChain.text: QatarEnergy extends LNG force majeure through end of December 2026 — 8th consecutive extension since April. Qatar LNG loadings pick up to roughly half of pre-war levels (Bloomberg, Nov 10). Global LNG supply gap estimated at ~600 bcf. Dutch TTF gas eased to ~€89.59/MWh (~$100.85), down from 4-year high above €101/MWh prior week; EU gas storage at 74.33% full vs 86% five-year average — lowest in over a decade entering winter (IEA). LNG crossings at Hormuz reached 32 in October — highest since war began (S&P Global). Pakistan to pay >$1B for winter LNG spot cargoes at ~2x Qatari contract price. Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda struck near Hormuz (Oct 31). Bangladesh struggling with spot market costs. Lufthansa says 2026 fuel costs €2B higher amid Iran war. Europe and Asia face tight supply heading into winter. JERA CEO says Qatar LNG supply unlikely to recover soon.

supplyChain.name: Petrochemicals
supplyChain.text: MEG ethylene/polyethylene exports disrupted. Gulf petrochem complex cut to ~60% capacity. Methanol down 80% (ITC). Dow, LyondellBasell margins widening on supply constraint. ExxonMobil Q3 profit more than doubled to $15.4B on energy surge. Aramco Q3 profit surges 34.6% to $36.3B.
